title: Add GitHub Actions RAG sandbox and contract-linter playbook
author: Maya Patel
description: Motivation: Provide a reproducible GitHub Actions sandbox for RAG quickstarts and a lightweight contract linter that validates tool-call schemas and structured output in CI. This enables (1) maintainers to verify quickstart compatibility on PRs, (2) authors to catch regression in tool contracts early, and (3) downstream teams to run smoke scenarios in ephemeral runners. What this PR adds: - A reusable Actions workflow (.github/workflows/rag-sandbox.yml) that spins up a matrix of Node/Python runners, provisions a local dev index (sqlite), downloads a pinned model artifact stub, and executes stepwise scenario smoke tests. - A contract linter (examples/rag-contract-linter/contract_linter.py) plus schema fixtures and a GitHub action wrapper to fail CI on contract/structured-output regressions. - An example sandbox workspace (examples/gha-sandbox/) with a compact README, step snapshots, a test harness (tests/smoke/gha-sandbox-smoke.spec), and a small runner script to emulate tool responses. - Shared telemetry probes and a minimal tracing shim so quickstarts emit consistent metrics used by the Console demo dashboards. - Doc updates: quickstart guide and authoring notes (docs/quickstarts/gha-rag-sandbox.md) describing local iteration, running the workflow, and how to author contract tests. Migration and scope: This is additive and opt-in for existing quickstarts. The GHA workflow is gated with a repo-level input and a small secrets matrix for private model artifacts. Checklist: - [x] Add Actions workflow and runner scripts - [x] Implement contract linter and schema examples - [x] Add smoke tests and example workspace - [x] Update quickstart docs and authoring notes - [x] Add telemetry probe YAML + example metrics - [x] Manual validation in a sandboxed fork (ran workflow with matrix: node14/node18 x python3.10/3.11) Security notes: - The workflow uses ephemeral runners and does not store secrets in artifacts. - Contract linter runs only on PRs and optionally on scheduled nightlies. Related tasks: Linear ENG-1324 implements the linter runner for other repos; PM-402 tracked on the quickstart UX copy and doc polish. How to try locally: - cd examples/gha-sandbox && ./action-runner.sh --local - For CI preview, see .github/workflows/rag-sandbox.yml and run via the Actions UI. Backwards compatibility: No breaking API changes. The linter can be enabled per-folder via a .contract-linter.yaml file.

Add contract_linter.py, schema fixtures, and action wrapper
Add smoke tests and telemetry probes; polish docs

review_comments: Jonah Lee: Nice end-to-end. Two requests: (1) make the linter fail-level configurable (warn vs fail); (2) add a short-circuit for flaky external calls so CI is deterministic.
Maya Patel (author): Made linter level configurable via .contract-linter.yaml and added a --offline switch for the runner to replay recorded tool responses.
Priya Singh: Please add clearer log output when schema mismatches occur (include path and example mismatch). Suggestion to include a sample GitHub Actions run link in the PR description.
Maya Patel: Updated error messages to include JSONPath and example snippet; added a run artifact link in the docs for demonstration.
Evan Carter: LGTM after minor nits; left an approval once the smoke test timeout was increased from 30s to 90s.
release_notes: Add a GitHub Actions sandbox workflow and a contract-linter quickstart to validate RAG examples in CI. Guides added to docs/quickstarts with local-run instructions and linter config reference.
docs_impact: Adds a new quickstart doc (gha-rag-sandbox) and expands authoring guidance for contract-driven tool calls. Includes example artifacts and screenshots for the docsite.
notes: This PR is intentionally self-contained — the linter is written to be re-used as a small GitHub Action across other example repos. Follow-up: wire the linter into redwood-quickstarts nightly matrix and add a small badge for contract status in README of each quickstart.
